writing.exampleCaption: The bound is exactly what `thread::spawn` asks for.
writing.explanation:
Send permits ownership transfer across threads. Sync means that a shared reference can be sent safely; formally, T is Sync when &T is Send. Auto-trait implementations depend on the fields and inner types, so Arc alone cannot make an arbitrary payload thread-safe.

`Send` allows ownership of a value to cross a thread boundary. `Sync` allows shared references to the value to be used from multiple threads; formally, `&T` is `Send` when `T` is `Sync`. These are marker traits, usually inferred from the fields of a type. A type may satisfy one but not the other. The distinction is about transfer versus shared access, so answer those as separate questions rather than saying a type is simply 'thread safe'.

`Rc<T>` is not suitable across threads because its reference count is non-atomic. `Arc<T>` uses an atomic reference count, so it can share ownership across threads when the contained `T` meets the required bounds. That does not make arbitrary mutation of `T` safe. If workers need to update one value, combine `Arc` with a mutex or use a narrower atomic operation. If they only read immutable data, `Arc` alone may suffice.

When the compiler rejects a value captured by `thread::spawn`, read whether the closure needs `Send`, whether a shared reference also needs `Sync`, and whether the captured value is owned or borrowed. Try moving a plain owned `String` first: transfer is fine. Then compare `Rc<String>` and `Arc<String>`. Do not add `unsafe impl Send` or `Sync` merely to satisfy a bound; those declarations promise safety to code you cannot inspect. The interview-quality answer gives both the trait definition and the design consequence.

writing.feedback: Arc<T> is Send and Sync only when the relevant T: Send + Sync bounds hold. Atomic reference counting alone does not make T thread-safe.

recall.question: Why can't worker threads share and mutate a counter through `Arc<RefCell<u32>>`, and what should you use instead?
recall.answer: `RefCell` tracks borrows with a non-atomic flag, so it is not `Sync`; the compiler rejects the `thread::spawn` because `RefCell<u32>` cannot be shared between threads (E0277). Use `Arc<Mutex<u32>>` or an `AtomicU32`.

recall.question: Why is adding `unsafe impl Send for MyType {}` a bad way to satisfy a failing `thread::spawn` bound?
recall.answer: It is a promise the compiler cannot check that every field is safe to transfer across threads. If the type holds something like an `Rc`, the promise is false and data races become possible; fix the design (move ownership, `Arc`, a lock) instead.

illustration.alt: Send allows moving a value to another thread; Sync allows shared references across threads.
illustration.caption: Send and Sync express different thread-safety promises.
